Verdict

Passed — 10.8 min of 25. Count correct, and candidate-verified for the first time in six attempts. 3 instructions · 262-word opener · 0 interrupts · 14 tool calls. The count half of the archetype was done properly; the model half was never attempted.

  • 6 · Domain vocabularyadequate

Requirement drift. The agent asked a two-part clarifying question and labelled one option in each “(Recommended)”. Both were accepted verbatim, with no words of the candidate's own. The second one removed the only model call from a model-tier problem. Attempt 001 flagged the identical pattern — this is a repeat finding.

Carry into the next attempt

  1. Say where each output comes from, in the opening instruction. “Caption: generate it with the cached BLIP captioner and print what it returns. shape_count: deterministic contour pass only — I won't ship a number that came out of a model's free text.”
  2. Treat “(Recommended)” as the agent's prior, not the spec. Ask: does this change what gets measured, or only how it gets built? When one option strictly dominates another for a few seconds of compute, take it.
  3. When you verify, state your number. Not “it is correct compared to my manual counting” but “I count 6 — 2 circles, 2 rectangles, 1 triangle, 1 arrow; your table matches.” An unfalsifiable claim buys none of the credit the real check earned.
  4. Finish the sentence after “I looked at the image”. Count it, give resolution and background, name the one object unlike the others. “etc.” is where this run's only bug was hiding.
